analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the need for further research on the specific mechanisms by which species-specific sequence variations and splicing isoforms of ANP32A influence the host restriction barrier for cross-species transmission. There is also a lack of detailed studies on the functional interactions between ANP32A and other host factors in the context of avian influenza.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should explore the molecular mechanisms of ANP32A in viral replication and host adaptation, particularly in relation to species-specific variations and splicing isoforms. Additionally, the development of targeted antiviral strategies that disrupt ANP32A-viral polymerase interactions could be a promising area for therapeutic intervention.

title_zh: 宿主 禽流感 病毒复制和跨物种适应中的 ANP32A 因子:叙述综述
source_body_en: Highly pathogenic avian influenza virus undergoes continuous evolution with strengthened cross-species transmission capacity, posing a severe threat to global public health security. Host acidic nuclear phosphoprotein 32A (ANP32A) acts as a critical host cofactor for activating influenza viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, and plays a central role in viral replication and host adaptation. This review systematically elaborates the molecular features of ANP32A, as well as the mechanism by which its leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domain specifically binds to the polymerase basic protein 2 (PB2) subunit and its low-complexity acidic region (LCAR) interacts with polymerase acidic protein (PA) to facilitate the assembly and functional activation of viral polymerase complexes. It also summarizes the influences of species-specific sequence variations and splicing isoforms of ANP32A on the host restriction barrier of cross-species transmission. Further analyses reveal that ANP32A indirectly modulates the transcriptional levels of genes related to interferons, NF-κB and NOD-like receptor pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasomes via chromatin epigenetic modification and transcriptional resource competition, remodeling the cellular antiviral microenvironment as a nuclear transcriptional regulator. ANP32A and acidic nuclear phosphoprotein 32B (ANP32B) exert complementary functions to support viral polymerase activity, while acidic nuclear phosphoprotein 32E (ANP32E) only provides weak auxiliary effects on a small subset of mutant influenza strains with its primary physiological function centered on chromatin regulation; the three proteins jointly participate in the regulatory network of viral replication. Drawing on recent advances in cryo-electron microscopy structural biology and CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing technologies, which are discussed narratively in this review, this review highlights the pivotal hub role of ANP32A in viral host adaptation and cross-species spillover.
abstract_zh: 高致病性禽流感病毒经历持续的进化,并增强了跨物种的传播能力,对全球公共卫生安全构成严重威胁。宿主 酸性核磷蛋白 32A (ANP32A) 作为激活流感病毒 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶的关键 宿主 辅因子,在病毒复制和 宿主 适应中发挥核心作用。该综述系统阐述了ANP32A的分子特征,及其富含亮氨酸重复序列(LRR)结构域特异性结合聚合酶碱性蛋白2(PB2)亚基及其低复杂性酸性区(LCAR)与聚合酶酸性蛋白(PA)相互作用以促进病毒聚合酶复合物组装和功能激活的机制。它还总结了ANP32A的物种特异性序列变异和剪接亚型对跨物种传播的宿主限制屏障的影响。进一步分析表明,ANP32A通过染色质表观遗传修饰和转录资源竞争,间接调节干扰素、NF-κB和NOD样受体pyrin结构域3(NLRP3)炎症小体相关基因的转录水平,重塑细胞抗病毒药物微环境作为核转录调节因子。ANP32A和酸性核磷蛋白32B(ANP32B)发挥互补功能支持病毒聚合酶活性,而酸性核磷蛋白32E(ANP32E)仅对一小部分突变流感毒株提供微弱的辅助作用,其主要生理功能以染色质调节为中心;这三种蛋白质共同参与病毒复制的调节网络。借鉴本综述中叙述性讨论的冷冻电镜结构生物学和 CRISPR/Cas9 基因编辑技术的最新进展,本综述强调了 ANP32A 在病毒 宿主 适应和跨物种 跨物种溢出 中的关键枢纽作用。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 宿主 因子 ANP32A 在 禽流感 病毒复制和跨物种适应中的作用。核心问题是ANP32A如何促进病毒复制并影响宿主 A病毒的宿主适应。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对现有文献的叙述性综合,讨论了 ANP32A 的分子特征、其与病毒聚合酶成分的相互作用,以及序列变异和剪接亚型对跨物种 传播 的影响。它不报告纳入研究的荟萃分析或具体资格标准。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: ANP32A 是一种关键的 宿主 辅因子,可激活流感病毒 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶,在病毒复制和 宿主 适应中发挥核心作用。其 LRR 结构域与 PB2 结合,其 LCAR 与 PA 相互作用,以促进病毒聚合酶复合物的组装和功能激活。此外,ANP32A 间接调节干扰素、NF-κB 和 NLRP3 炎性体相关基因的转录水平,重塑细胞 抗病毒药物 微环境。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调需要进一步研究 ANP32A 的物种特异性序列变异和剪接亚型影响跨物种 传播 的 宿主 限制屏障的具体机制。在 禽流感 背景下,还缺乏对 ANP32A 与其他 宿主 因子之间功能相互作用的详细研究。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应探索 ANP32A 在病毒复制和 宿主 适应中的分子机制,特别是与物种特异性变异和剪接亚型相关的分子机制。此外,开发破坏 ANP32A-病毒聚合酶相互作用的靶向 抗病毒药物 策略可能是治疗干预的一个有前景的领域。

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of PCR-Based Methods for Avian Influenza Virus Detection: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: This study aims to systematically review and meta-analyze the diagnostic accuracy of polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based methods for the detection of avian influenza virus (AIV). With the ongoing threat of avian influenza outbreaks to both poultry industries and public health, accurate and rapid diagnostic tools are critical for early detection, surveillance, and outbreak control. This systematic review will evaluate the sensitivity, specificity, and overall diagnostic performance of various PCR-based assays (including RT-PCR, real-time RT-PCR, and multiplex PCR) compared to reference standards such as viral isolation and serological testing. Studies will be identified through comprehensive searches of electronic databases (e.g., PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase). The findings of this meta-analysis will provide evidence-based insights into the most reliable PCR-based diagnostic methods for AIV detection, informing clinical and veterinary diagnostic practices, as well as public health surveillance strategies.

title: Rare Adenoviral Vectored Vaccines for Emerging Influenza Threats
abstract: Background: Emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases pose a growing global threat, underscoring the need for vaccine platforms enabling rapid deployment and durable, broad protection. Although mRNA and viral vector vaccines transformed pandemic responses, limitations include waning immunity, restricted antigenic breadth, pre-existing vector immunity, and rare vector-associated adverse events. Here, we evaluate recombinant adenovirus serotypes 4, 28, and 48 expressing a centralized H5 influenza hemagglutinin consensus antigen as next-generation vectors for broad, single-dose protection against diverse H5 influenza clades. Methods: An H5 centralized consensus vaccine was designed using human sequences from the 2003–2006 bird flu outbreak and cloned into four low-prevalence recombinant adenoviruses. Mice received a single intramuscular or intranasal vaccination and were challenged two weeks later with high doses of diverse, lethal, reverse-genetics-derived H5N1 viruses. Immune correlates, survival, and protection from challenge-associated weight loss were assessed. Results: Vaccinated mice were largely protected from lethal challenge against strains spanning twenty years of influenza evolution. Both vaccination routes conferred complete protection against antigenically related strains, and strong protection against more divergent clade 2.3.4.4b strains. Protection occurred before neutralizing antibodies could be detected, although strong H5 antibody responses were induced by all vaccines. Intramuscular vaccination generated strong serum IgG and antigen-specific T cell responses, while intranasal vaccination promoted robust antigen-specific mucosal IgA production. Conclusions: Adenovirus vectors expressing a centralized H5 consensus hemagglutinin elicit rapid, broad protection against diverse H5 influenza viruses following a single intramuscular or intranasal immunization. These results support the continued development of low-seroprevalence adenoviral vectors as a next-generation influenza vaccine platform for rapidly emerging influenza viruses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 新出现和重新出现的传染病构成了日益严重的全球威胁,凸显了对 疫苗 平台的需求,该平台能够实现快速部署和持久、广泛的保护。尽管mRNA和病毒媒介 疫苗改变了大流行反应,但其局限性包括免疫力减弱、抗原宽度受限、预先存在的媒介免疫力以及罕见的媒介相关不良事件。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 2003-2006 年禽流感 暴发 的人类序列设计了 H5 集中共识 疫苗,并将其克隆到四种低 患病率 重组腺病毒中。小鼠接受单次肌内或鼻内 疫苗接种 注射,两周后接受高剂量的多种、致命、反向遗传学衍生的 H5N1 病毒的攻击。
elements_zh.methods: 评估了免疫相关性、存活率以及对挑战相关体重减轻的保护。表达集中 H5 共有血凝素的腺病毒 媒介 在单次肌内或鼻内免疫后可针对多种 H5 流感病毒产生快速、广泛的保护。
elements_zh.main_results: 接种疫苗的小鼠在很大程度上免受针对跨越二十年的流感 进化 毒株的致命攻击。尽管所有 疫苗 均诱导了强烈的 H5 抗体反应,但在检测到中和抗体之前就发生了保护作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 两种 疫苗接种 途径均提供针对抗原相关菌株的完全保护,以及针对更趋异的进化枝 2.3.4.4b 菌株的强力保护。肌内注射 疫苗接种 产生强烈的血清 IgG 和抗原特异性 T 细胞反应,而鼻内注射 疫苗接种 则促进强劲的抗原特异性粘膜 IgA 产生。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果支持低 血清流行率 腺病毒 媒介 作为下一代流感 疫苗 平台的持续开发,用于快速出现的流感病毒。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据不报告设计限制、偏见、混杂、样本量、对照、普遍性或仅抽象的证据。证据强度很高,因为它基于受控实验环境中的直接观察。

abstract_zh: 背景:新兴和再新兴的传染病对全球构成日益严重的威胁,凸显了需要疫苗平台以实现快速部署和持久、广泛的保护的必要性。尽管mRNA和病毒媒介 疫苗改变了大流行应对方式,但其局限性包括免疫力减弱、抗原广度受限、预先存在的媒介免疫力以及罕见的媒介相关不良事件。在此,我们评估了表达集中化H5流感血凝素共识抗原的重组腺病毒血清型4、28和48作为下一代媒介,以实现对多种H5流感亚型的广泛、单剂量保护。方法:利用2003–2006年禽流感暴发的人类序列设计了一种H5集中化共识疫苗,并将其克隆到四种低患病率的重组腺病毒中。小鼠通过单次肌肉或鼻内接种疫苗接种,并在两周后接受多种高剂量、致死性的逆转录遗传学衍生H5N1病毒的挑战。评估了免疫相关指标、存活率以及挑战相关体重减轻的保护效果。结果:接种疫苗的小鼠对跨越二十年的流感进化亚型的致死性挑战表现出广泛的保护。两种疫苗接种接种途径均对抗原相关亚型提供了完全保护,并对更远源的2.3.4.4b亚型提供了强效保护。保护作用在中和抗体可检测之前就已经发生,尽管所有疫苗均诱导了强烈的H5抗体反应。肌肉接种疫苗接种产生了强效的血清IgG和抗原特异性T细胞反应,而鼻内接种疫苗接种则促进了强效的抗原特异性黏膜IgA产生。结论:表达集中化H5共识血凝素的腺病毒媒介在单次肌肉或鼻内免疫后可快速、广泛地保护机体免受多种H5流感病毒的侵害。这些结果支持继续开发低血清流行率的腺病毒媒介作为应对快速出现的流感病毒的下一代流感疫苗平台。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果支持低 血清流行率 腺病毒 媒介 作为下一代流感 疫苗 平台的持续开发,用于快速出现的流感病毒。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据不报告设计限制、偏见、混杂、样本量、对照、普遍性或仅抽象的证据。证据强度很高,因为它基于受控实验环境中的直接观察。

title: Beyond the Limits: Sequencing A/H5N1 from Animal Tissues with Low Viral Loads
abstract: Recent reports indicate a growing number of A/H5N1 infections in companion animals and wildlife, particularly across Europe and the United States and, most recently, in Australia, where the virus poses a potentially serious threat to endemic wildlife, including threatened species. In Poland, following an epizootic that occurred in summer 2023, A/H5N1 virus has continued to be detected in domestic animals showing clinical signs. Continued occurrence of mammalian infections remains possible, underscoring the need for reliable diagnostic approaches. Our experience suggests that A/H5N1 infection can remain challenging to diagnose even in animals with severe clinical signs and rapidly progressive, often fatal disease. In selected clinical and post-mortem samples, low viral RNA loads and/or the presence of tissue-derived PCR inhibitors can hamper amplification and subsequent sequencing. Nevertheless, by mid-2026, we had identified more than 40 A/H5N1 infections in dogs, cats, and ferrets, highlighting the continued need for sensitive molecular diagnostic approaches in mammalian cases. The optimized workflow enables robust downstream targeted Sanger sequencing of hemagglutinin (H5) and neuraminidase (N1) amplicons, providing a rapid diagnostic rescue approach for subtype confirmation and targeted genetic characterization. By refining diagnostic workflows for low-viral-load samples, this protocol enables molecular diagnostic confirmation of HPAI H5N1 subtype in companion animals.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the challenge of diagnosing A/H5N1 infections in companion animals and wildlife, particularly in cases with low viral loads. The research highlights the continued presence of A/H5N1 in domestic animals in Poland following an epizootic in 2023, emphasizing the need for sensitive diagnostic methods. The authors describe an optimized workflow that enables targeted Sanger sequencing of hemagglutinin (H5) and neuraminidase (N1) amplicons, offering a rapid diagnostic approach for subtype confirmation. Their findings suggest that A/H5N1 can be difficult to diagnose even in animals with severe clinical signs. The study's significance lies in its contribution to improving diagnostic capabilities for HPAI H5N1 in mammalian hosts. The evidence is based on observational data from clinical and post-mortem samples, and the study does not report specific limitations or evidence strength assessment.

title: From Dietary Proteins to Antiviral Peptides: Machine Learning-Guided Discovery and Structural Evaluation Against H5N1 Influenza Polymerase
abstract: Food proteins are well-known bioactive peptides, but their inhibitory activities against the influenza H5N1 polymerase have not been widely studied. In this paper, we applied a computational pipeline to predict the antiviral activities of food-derived peptides against the PB1 subunit of H5N1 polymerase. Nineteen proteins from soybean, cow milk, egg, pea, maize, rice, and cowpea were analyzed in terms of their physiochemical properties, allergenicity, and antimicrobial and hemolytic activities, and then digested in silico with pepsin and chymotrypsin. The peptides generated from each digestion process were ranked according to their antiviral activities using four different machine learning algorithms (SVM, Random Forest, IBk, and K-Star) and prioritized on the basis of consensus across multiple models as well as gastrointestinal release and non-hemolytic properties. Peptides chosen were docked to PB1 protein on three independent docking servers (HawkDock, PatchDock, and pyDockWEB) and further analyzed in terms of interaction analysis and MD simulations with 200.4 ns. Some proteins exhibited a high score for antimicrobial activity, such as legumin A (0.970), β-conglycinin α subunit (0.941), and glutelin type-A 1 (0.911). Most proteins were similar to known allergens. The peptides that showed consistent results in terms of antiviral properties and docking include RIQQAIAAGILPLSPL, SSAVSSVCENPILQPY, and QPYRIQQAI-AAGILPL, even though the ranking of their efficacy by both platforms was different. The peptide SSAVSSVCENPILQPY is the most consistent candidate for further research and has 29 close contacts and four hydrogen bonds. In addition, the complex formed between it and PB1 is stable throughout the simulation period. These results allow identifying peptide candidates for further investigation, but all of them are based only on computational results. They need to be proven experimentally.

title: Geospatial evidence of introduction of highly pathogenic avian influenza into dairy farms in the United States
abstract: The emergence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) A/H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has led to unprecedented intercontinental spread spread across avian and mammalian species. First confirmed outbreaks in dairy farms happened in the United States in March 2024. This study evaluated the modes of introduction and spread across 42 confirmed dairy farm outbreaks spanning nine states between 10 March and 5 May 2024, through geospatial mapping, case-control ecological exposure analysis, and space-time cluster testing. Non-waterfowl abundance was significantly higher in outbreak counties than in high-cattle-density non-outbreak counties (p<0.00001, r=-0.542), identifying it as a distinguishing ecological feature of early dairy outbreak locations. Knox space-time cluster analysis confirmed non-random transmission dynamics across 14 of 30 threshold combinations, consistent with a single introduction in Texas followed by regional and trade-mediated amplification, with livestock trade, poultry litter, and contaminated milking equipment as likely contributing factors. Proactive surveillance targeting counties with high non-waterfowl abundance and cattle density is essential to reduce the risk of further spillover events.

title: Probiotics as a Strategy for Mitigating Viral Infections in Poultry: Immunomodulatory Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.
abstract: Poultry viral infections remain a persistent challenge for the poultry industry, causing significant economic losses and posing potential threats to human health. The escalating frequency of outbreaks involving pathogens, such as infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), Newcastle disease virus (NDV) and avian influenza virus (AIV), underscores the urgent need for effective interventions. Probiotics have gained attention as a promising strategy to combat these viral infections due to their potential in enhancing immune responses and establishing a healthy gut microbiome. A literature search was carried out on Google Scholar, Scopus and PubMed using key search terms, such as 'probiotics', 'Lactobacillus', 'acidophilus', 'poultry', 'viral infections', 'Newcastle Disease Virus (NDV)' and other relevant terms. Inclusion criteria for manuscripts used were based on the relevance to probiotic-based interventions in poultry, the focus on immunological mechanisms and the examination of viral pathogens commonly found in West African poultry farming systems. This review explores the role of probiotics in mitigating the effects of NDV, AIV and IBV in poultry, focusing on their immunomodulatory effects and antiviral mechanisms. Lactobacillus acidophilus, L. plantarum have shown an interesting promise in countering NDV infections by modulating immunological parameters and enhancing antibody responses. Similarly, these probiotics have exhibited antiviral activity against AIV, promoting immune activation and reducing viral loads. plantarum have emerged as potential adjuvants for IBV vaccines, improving antibody responses and humoural immunity.

title_original: Probiotics as a Strategy for Mitigating Viral Infections in Poultry: Immunomodulatory Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the use of probiotics to mitigate viral infections in poultry, particularly avian influenza A viruses, by examining their immunomodulatory effects and antiviral mechanisms. The central question is whether probiotics can serve as an effective strategy for reducing the impact of these viruses on poultry health and potentially human health through zoonotic transmission.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a literature search on Google Scholar, Scopus, and PubMed using terms like 'probiotics', 'Lactobacillus', 'acidophilus', 'poultry', 'viral infections', 'Newcastle Disease Virus (NDV)', and other relevant terms. Inclusion criteria were based on the relevance to probiotic-based interventions in poultry, the focus on immunological mechanisms, and the examination of viral pathogens common in West African poultry farming systems.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Probiotics, particularly Lactobacillus acidophilus and Lactobacillus plantarum, have shown potential in modulating immunological parameters, enhancing antibody responses, and reducing viral loads against avian influenza A viruses (AIV). These findings suggest that probiotics may be a viable strategy for improving immune defenses against AIV in poultry.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the need for more targeted studies on probiotics' effects against specific avian influenza subtypes, such as H5N1 and H5N6. There is limited evidence on the long-term efficacy of probiotics in preventing zoonotic transmission of AIV to humans, and further research is required to address these gaps.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize investigating the efficacy of probiotics against specific avian influenza subtypes and their role in preventing zoonotic transmission. Practical applications may include integrating probiotics into poultry farming practices to enhance immune responses and reduce the economic and public health burden of AIV outbreaks.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the potential of probiotics, particularly Lactobacillus acidophilus and Lactobacillus plantarum, in mitigating avian influenza A virus (AIV) infections in poultry. It highlights their immunomodulatory effects and antiviral properties, suggesting they may enhance immune defenses and reduce viral loads. However, the review identifies gaps in understanding the long-term efficacy of probiotics against specific AIV subtypes and their role in zoonotic transmission. The findings support further research into targeted probiotic interventions and their integration into poultry farming practices to improve health outcomes and reduce economic losses associated with AIV outbreaks.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述的重点是通过检查益生菌的免疫调节作用和 抗病毒药物 机制,使用益生菌减轻家禽病毒感染,特别是 禽流感 A 病毒。核心问题是益生菌是否可以作为一种有效策略,通过人畜共患 传播 来减少这些病毒对家禽健康和潜在人类健康的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述使用“益生菌”、“乳杆菌”、“嗜酸菌”、“家禽”、“病毒感染”、“新城疫病毒 (NDV)”等术语和其他相关术语在 Google Scholar、Scopus 和 PubMed 上进行了文献检索。纳入标准基于与家禽益生菌干预措施的相关性、对免疫机制的关注以及对西非家禽养殖系统中常见病毒病原体的检查。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 益生菌,特别是嗜酸乳杆菌和植物乳杆菌,已显示出调节免疫参数、增强抗体反应和减少针对 禽流感 A 病毒 (AIV) 的病毒载量的潜力。这些发现表明,益生菌可能是改善家禽 AIV 免疫防御的可行策略。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调需要对益生菌针对特定 禽流感 亚型(例如 H5N1 和 H5N6)的作用进行更有针对性的研究。关于益生菌在预防人类 AIV 人畜共患 传播 方面的长期功效的证据有限,需要进一步研究来解决这些差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应优先研究益生菌对特定 禽流感 亚型的功效及其在预防人畜共患 传播 中的作用。实际应用可能包括将益生菌融入家禽养殖实践中,以增强 免疫应答 并减少 AIV 暴发 的经济和公共卫生负担。

abstract_zh: 禽类病毒感染仍然是禽类养殖业中的持续挑战,导致显著的经济损失并可能对人类健康构成潜在威胁。涉及病原体的病毒感染频率不断上升,例如传染性支气管炎病毒(IBV)、新城疫病毒(NDV)和禽流感病毒(AIV),凸显了对有效干预措施的迫切需求。由于益生菌在增强免疫应答和建立健康肠道微生物群方面具有潜力,它们已成为一种有前景的策略,用于对抗这些病毒感染。通过在Google Scholar、Scopus和PubMed上使用关键搜索词,如'益生菌'、'乳酸杆菌'、'嗜酸乳杆菌'、'禽类'、'病毒感染'、'新城疫病毒(NDV)'及其他相关术语进行了文献检索。所选文献的纳入标准基于其与禽类益生菌干预措施的相关性、对免疫机制的关注以及对西非禽类养殖系统中常见病毒病原体的分析。本综述探讨了益生菌在减轻NDV、AIV和IBV对禽类影响中的作用,重点在于其免疫调节效应和抗病毒机制。嗜酸乳杆菌(Lactobacillus acidophilus)和植物乳杆菌(L. plantarum)在调节免疫参数和增强抗体反应方面显示出对抗NDV感染的有趣前景。同样,这些益生菌在对抗AIV方面也表现出抗病毒活性,促进免疫激活并降低病毒载量。植物乳杆菌在应对IBV病毒感染方面已显示出潜在的辅助作用,改善抗体反应和体液免疫。

title: Differentiating Avian and Seasonal Influenza Viruses in Wastewater by Digital PCR
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5Nx) viruses, particularly clade 2.3.4.4b, pose substantial global health risks. We combined and piloted 2 duplex reverse transcription digital PCRs to discriminate between avian and seasonal influenza viruses in wastewater. This approach enabled rapid, strain-specific detection to reduce ambiguity in environmental surveillance for influenza viruses.

title: Climate Change Impacts to Bald Eagles (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) Within the Great Lakes Region
abstract: The Bald Eagle is one of the most studied birds in North America, and Michigan’s population has been studied extensively since 1961. They have faced many challenges to their survival. From bounty hunting, to egg-shell thinning caused by DDT, to the more recent population loss caused by the outbreak of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza, many stressors threaten their population. Bald Eagles are also impacted by the effects of global climate change. Climate change impacts on their populations are not well known, including the impacts of warming temperatures and extreme weather events. Two studies were conducted to determine the extent of these impacts to Michigan’s population of Bald Eagles. The first study examined how Bergmann’s rule–stating that within a species individuals found closer to the poles are larger than those closer to the equator–may be impacted in Bald Eagles with warming temperatures. This study utilized morphometrics data collected from nestlings banded in Michigan from 1999–2025, and from nestlings banded at Voyageurs National Park in Minnesota from 2011–2025 to examine if nestling size has changed over time and with temperature. Additionally, in the event that nestlings are changing in size with time or temperature, we sought to examine the efficacy of the continued use of the footpad method for sex determination in the field. We did so by comparing sex as determined by the footpad and sex as determined by DNA analysis. Analyses of nestling measurements revealed significant decreases over time in many subsets of the population, however very few subsets showed significant changes in measurements with temperature over time, with most showing increases in size and one showing a decrease in size. In many subsets with significant changes in measurements with temperature, there is no significance in change of measurements over time, suggesting some change may be as a result of developmental plasticity and not evolutionary adaptation. Analysis of footpad versus DNA determined sex revealed that the footpad method is still moderately accurate. Continued use of this method in the field should be used with caution, and we should consider the ability to sex individuals using DNA in the future for improved accuracy. The second study examined the impacts to Bald Eagle activity, productivity, and nest tree health from a severe ice storm in the northern lower peninsula of Michigan in March 2025. The storm caused ice to quickly accumulate on natural and man-made structures, leaving over 1,100 km of roads impassable, and damaging over 1.2 million hectares of forest land, including eagle nest trees. Analysis of impacts was achieved via aerial surveys that quantified damage to nesting trees and recorded activity and productivity of known nest sites. An additional goal was to model damage to nest trees not surveyed, and to assess the accuracy of the aerial surveys and model via ground surveys. We found a large decrease in the activity of breeding pairs and productivity of nests within the impacted areas following the storm, with over 50% of the impacted breeding pairs failing to raise young. Even nests without damage to the nest tree experienced failure. Many nests which had young prior to the storm were found empty after, confirming that the storm caused mortality in some nests. Ground-truthing observations indicated that damage to nest trees was underestimated during aerial surveys due to the inability of pilots to see branches directly beneath the nest bowl, highlighting that damage was likely more severe than what was initially observed aerially. The ground surveys also showed that the model was only correct in predicting damage to 40% of the nest trees not surveyed, and that areas not surveyed still received severe damage. These studies demonstrate that Bald Eagles are impacted by climate change, oftentimes negatively, and demonstrate the importance of long-term monitoring of wildlife species. This is increasingly important as climate change impacts grow in magnitude and frequency. Additionally, these studies establish a replicable methodology for raptor population monitoring for Bergmann’s Rule analyses and for population monitoring following acute adverse weather events.

title: Update to the CDC influenza A(H3) subtyping assay for improved detection of influenza A(H3N2) viruses, including subclade K viruses
abstract: ABSTRACT Influenza A(H3N2) viruses circulate globally and cause respiratory illness. The FDA-cleared CDC Human Influenza Virus Real-Time RT-PCR Influenza A (H3/H1pdm09) Subtyping assay is used to subtype seasonal influenza A viruses. However, emerging mutations in the H3 reverse primer region raised concerns about reduced assay sensitivity for contemporary circulating viruses. We updated the H3 assay by redesigning the reverse primer to target a more conserved region of the hemagglutinin gene, and incorporating minor adjustments into the forward primer and probe. Analytical sensitivity, inclusivity, and exclusivity evaluations were performed using cultured influenza viruses, synthetic RNA, and panels of non-influenza respiratory pathogens. Clinical performance was evaluated using seasonal A(H3N2) residual respiratory specimens. The updated assay (H3_v2) demonstrated analytical sensitivity comparable to or improved over the initial H3 assay, with a limit of detection of approximately 10 1.7 –10 2.1 EID 50 /mL and five copies of RNA per reaction. Improved performance was observed for viruses containing A21G with T23G, T23C, or T23A double mismatches in the reverse primer, with a measurable Ct value shift between the initial H3 and H3_v2 assay. The assay showed 100% agreement with expected results in 139 clinical specimens, and no cross-reactivity with other influenza subtypes or other respiratory pathogens. These findings indicate the updated H3_v2 assay improves sensitivity for contemporary and emerging seasonal A(H3N2) viruses while maintaining high specificity. This update ensures continued reliable detection of seasonal A(H3N2), including genetically drifted A(H3N2) viruses, such as the recently emerged A(H3N2) subclade K viruses, and supports global influenza surveillance and diagnostic preparedness. IMPORTANCE Accurate detection and subtyping of influenza A(H3N2) viruses are essential for clinical diagnostics, outbreak response, and global influenza surveillance. The emergence and fixation of mutations leading to primer mismatches in the FDA-cleared CDC A(H3) real-time RT-PCR assay raised concerns about reduced sensitivity for contemporary circulating A(H3N2) viruses. To address this, we redesigned the reverse primer and optimized additional assay components to improve detection of currently circulating seasonal A(H3N2) viruses. The updated H3_v2 assay restores and enhances sensitivity, including for viruses harboring key reverse primer mismatches, while maintaining high specificity and complete agreement with clinical specimens. This update ensures reliable detection of seasonal influenza A(H3N2) and A(H3N2) variant viruses, including recently emerged A(H3N2) subclade K viruses, and strengthens diagnostic preparedness and surveillance capacity nationally and internationally.

title: Hematologic and biochemical prognostic indicators of influenza disease severity in naïve and preimmune ferret (Mustela putorius furo) models
abstract: Abstract Ferrets ( Mustela putorius furo ) are widely used to evaluate influenza virus pathogenicity and pandemic risk, but hematologic and biochemical parameters are not routinely included in these assessments. In this study, we performed a comparative analysis of complete blood count and serum chemistry profiles in immunologically naïve and preimmune ferrets following intranasal inoculation with different influenza virus strains. Seasonal A(H1N1)pdm09 and A(H3N2) viruses and a less virulent A(H5N1) virus caused mild, nonfatal disease with limited or transient bloodwork changes in naïve ferrets. In contrast, naïve ferrets challenged with a highly virulent A(H5N1) virus showed virus detection beyond the upper respiratory tract, rapid disease progression accompanied by pronounced metabolic and biochemical disruption, necessitating humane euthanasia. Pre-existing immunity altered disease progression following challenge with this virus, with A(H1N1)pdm09-preimmune ferrets displaying reduced viral replication, less severe disease, and less pronounced biochemical disruption compared to A(H3N2)-preimmune ferrets. Overall, lymphopenia was common during acute infection in both ferret models; however, it did not distinguish nonfatal from fatal disease. Conversely, worsening biochemical changes, including hyperglycemia, increased alanine aminotransferase, total bilirubin, amylase, globulin, and electrolyte disturbances, were most evident in ferrets with severe A(H5N1) disease. These findings support the use of serial hematologic and serum chemistry analyses as complementary endpoints for evaluating disease severity, immune-mediated protection, and humane endpoint decisions in naïve and preimmune ferret models.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate hematologic and biochemical indicators of influenza disease severity in naïve and preimmune ferret models, addressing the gap in routine assessments of these parameters for influenza virus pathogenicity and pandemic risk.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compared complete blood count and serum chemistry profiles in immunologically naïve and preimmune ferrets following intranasal inoculation with different influenza virus strains, including seasonal A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and a highly virulent A(H5N1) virus.
analysis.methods: The researchers conducted a comparative analysis of hematologic and biochemical parameters in ferrets, using intranasal inoculation with various influenza virus strains and monitoring changes in bloodwork and disease progression.
analysis.main_results: Naïve ferrets infected with a highly virulent A(H5N1) virus showed virus detection beyond the upper respiratory tract, rapid disease progression, and pronounced metabolic and biochemical disruption, requiring humane euthanasia. Preimmune ferrets had reduced viral replication, less severe disease, and less pronounced biochemical changes compared to A(H3N2)-preimmune ferrets.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that hematologic and biochemical changes are more pronounced in severe A(H5N1) infections, highlighting their potential as complementary endpoints for assessing disease severity and immune protection in ferret models.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results suggest that serial hematologic and serum chemistry analyses could improve the evaluation of disease severity and immune responses in ferret models, aiding in the development of better surveillance and intervention strategies for avian influenza.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to ferret models and does not include human data, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on observational findings in a controlled animal model.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates hematologic and biochemical indicators of influenza disease severity in naïve and preimmune ferret models. It highlights that highly virulent A(H5N1) virus causes severe disease with pronounced metabolic and biochemical disruption, while preimmune ferrets show reduced viral replication and less severe outcomes. The findings suggest that these parameters could serve as complementary endpoints for assessing disease severity and immune protection in ferret models, which are important for evaluating avian influenza. However, the study is limited to animal models and does not include human data, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on observational findings in a controlled setting.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估幼稚和免疫前雪貂模型中流感疾病严重程度的血液学和生化指标,弥补流感病毒致病性和大流行风险的这些参数的常规评估中的差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究比较了鼻内接种不同流感病毒株(包括季节性 A(H1N1)pdm09、A(H3N2) 和高毒力 A(H5N1) 病毒)后,未免疫雪貂和免疫前雪貂的全血细胞计数和血清化学特征。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员通过鼻内接种各种流感病毒株并监测血液工作和疾病进展的变化,对雪貂的血液学和生化参数进行了比较分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 感染高毒力 A(H5N1) 病毒的幼雪貂表现出上呼吸道以外的病毒检测、疾病进展迅速以及明显的代谢和生化破坏,需要人道安乐死。与 A(H3N2) 免疫前雪貂相比,免疫前雪貂的病毒复制减少,疾病较轻,生化变化也不太明显。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,在严重的 A(H5N1) 感染中,血液学和生化变化更为明显,凸显了它们作为雪貂模型中评估疾病严重程度和免疫保护的补充终点的潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明,连续血液学和血清化学分析可以改善雪貂模型中疾病严重程度和 免疫应答 的评估,有助于制定更好的 监测 和 禽流感 干预策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于雪貂模型,不包括人类数据,这可能会影响普遍性。证据是中等的,因为它是基于受控动物模型的观察结果。

In this study, we performed a comparative analysis of complete blood count and serum chemistry profiles in immunologically naïve and preimmune ferrets following intranasal inoculation with different influenza virus strains. Seasonal A(H1N1)pdm09 and A(H3N2) viruses and a less virulent A(H5N1) virus caused mild, nonfatal disease with limited or transient bloodwork changes in naïve ferrets. In contrast, naïve ferrets challenged with a highly virulent A(H5N1) virus showed virus detection beyond the upper respiratory tract, rapid disease progression accompanied by pronounced metabolic and biochemical disruption, necessitating humane euthanasia. Pre-existing immunity altered disease progression following challenge with this virus, with A(H1N1)pdm09-preimmune ferrets displaying reduced viral replication, less severe disease, and less pronounced biochemical disruption compared to A(H3N2)-preimmune ferrets. Overall, lymphopenia was common during acute infection in both ferret models; however, it did not distinguish nonfatal from fatal disease. Conversely, worsening biochemical changes, including hyperglycemia, increased alanine aminotransferase, total bilirubin, amylase, globulin, and electrolyte disturbances, were most evident in ferrets with severe A(H5N1) disease. These findings support the use of serial hematologic and serum chemistry analyses as complementary endpoints for evaluating disease severity, immune-mediated protection, and humane endpoint decisions in naïve and preimmune ferret models.
abstract_zh: 摘要 雪貂 ( Mustela putorius furo ) 被广泛用于评估流感病毒的致病性和大流行风险,但这些评估中通常不包括血液学和生化参数。在这项研究中,我们对鼻内接种不同流感病毒株后的免疫学幼稚雪貂和免疫前雪貂的全血细胞计数和血清化学特征进行了比较分析。季节性 A(H1N1)pdm09 和 A(H3N2) 病毒以及毒性较低的 A(H5N1) 病毒会导致幼雪貂出现轻微的非致命性疾病,并伴有有限或短暂的血液检查变化。相比之下,接受高毒力 A(H5N1) 病毒攻击的幼稚雪貂表现出上呼吸道以外的病毒检测,疾病进展迅速,伴随着明显的代谢和生化破坏,需要人道安乐死。预先存在的免疫力改变了受到该病毒攻击后的疾病进展,与 A(H3N2) 免疫前雪貂相比,A(H1N1)pdm09 免疫前雪貂表现出病毒复制减少、疾病不那么严重以及生化破坏不那么明显。总体而言,两种雪貂模型在急性感染期间淋巴细胞减少都很常见。然而,它没有区分非致命疾病和致命疾病。相反,恶化的生化变化,包括高血糖、丙氨酸氨基转移酶、总胆红素、淀粉酶、球蛋白和电解质紊乱增加,在患有严重甲型H5N1疾病的雪貂中最为明显。这些发现支持使用连续血液学和血清化学分析作为评估疾病严重程度、免疫介导的保护以及幼稚和免疫前雪貂模型中的人道终点决策的补充终点。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估幼稚和免疫前雪貂模型中流感疾病严重程度的血液学和生化指标,弥补流感病毒致病性和大流行风险的这些参数的常规评估中的差距。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究比较了鼻内接种不同流感病毒株(包括季节性 A(H1N1)pdm09、A(H3N2) 和高毒力 A(H5N1) 病毒)后,未免疫雪貂和免疫前雪貂的全血细胞计数和血清化学特征。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员通过鼻内接种各种流感病毒株并监测血液工作和疾病进展的变化,对雪貂的血液学和生化参数进行了比较分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 感染高毒力 A(H5N1) 病毒的幼雪貂表现出上呼吸道以外的病毒检测、疾病进展迅速以及明显的代谢和生化破坏,需要人道安乐死。与 A(H3N2) 免疫前雪貂相比,免疫前雪貂的病毒复制减少,疾病较轻,生化变化也不太明显。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,在严重的 A(H5N1) 感染中,血液学和生化变化更为明显,凸显了它们作为雪貂模型中评估疾病严重程度和免疫保护的补充终点的潜力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明,连续血液学和血清化学分析可以改善雪貂模型中疾病严重程度和 免疫应答 的评估,有助于制定更好的 监测 和 禽流感 干预策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于雪貂模型,不包括人类数据,这可能会影响普遍性。证据是中等的,因为它是基于受控动物模型的观察结果。

title: Single-Tube Six-Channel Ultrafast PCR with Melting-Curve Discrimination for Seven Respiratory Pathogens.
abstract: Expanding single-tube multiplexing beyond the number of fluorescence channels on a real-time PCR instrument is a persistent challenge for point-of-care testing (POCT). Here, we break this barrier by leveraging melting temperature (Tm) as an extra information dimension. By employing a probe-cleavage-mediated reporter-duplex strategy, we circumvent the conventional limitation that hydrolyzed TaqMan probes cannot participate in postamplification melting analysis. Two FAM-labeled probes, each containing an engineered 5'-terminal nontarget extension, generate cleavage-dependent reporter amplicons with distinctly different melting temperatures (ΔTm = 10.3 °C), enabling precise differentiation between BV (72.5 °C) and BY (82.8 °C) within a single optical channel. Combined with a lyophilized-bead cartridge that automates nucleic acid release (4 min) and an ultrafast PCR run (16 min), the platform detects eight targets─seven respiratory pathogens (SARS-CoV-2, influenza A H1N1/H3N2/H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, influenza B Victoria/Yamagata, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae) plus one internal control (B2M)─using only six optical channels. The assay achieves a limit of detection of 5 copies per reaction (R2 > 0.97, amplification efficiency 96-104%) with no cross-reactivity against 55 nontarget microorganisms, and intra/inter-assay CVs < 5%. The lyophilized beads remain stable for 12 months at 25 °C (ΔCt < 1.5). In 272 clinical throat swabs, the system shows 100% agreement with single-plex qPCR. Mixed BV/BY infections produce two distinct melting peaks, with the low-abundance peak detectable down to a 400:1 ratio under the tested conditions. This six-channel ultrafast PCR system reliably detects eight targets in one tube within 20 min without extra hardware, providing a generic strategy for higher-order multiplexing in point-of-care settings.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of expanding single-tube multiplexing beyond the number of fluorescence channels on a real-time PCR instrument, which is a persistent issue for point-of-care testing (POCT).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a six-channel ultrafast PCR system designed to detect seven respiratory pathogens, including avian influenza A virus subtypes, in a single tube using clinical throat swab specimens collected from 272 patients.
analysis.methods: The method involved a probe-cleavage-mediated reporter-duplex strategy that allows for the detection of multiple targets using melting-curve discrimination, combined with a lyophilized-bead cartridge that automates nucleic acid release and an ultrafast PCR run.
analysis.main_results: The system demonstrated 100% agreement with single-plex qPCR in 272 clinical throat swabs, and it can detect mixed infections of BV and BY with two distinct melting peaks, even at a 400:1 ratio.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret this as a reliable and efficient platform for detecting multiple respiratory pathogens in one tube within 20 minutes, offering a novel strategy for higher-order multiplexing in point-of-care settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more efficient and accurate diagnostic tools for avian influenza A viruses and other respiratory pathogens in clinical and field settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on an abstract-only report, and the study does not provide detailed statistical analyses or long-term performance data beyond 12 months of stability.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a six-channel ultrafast PCR system that enables the detection of seven respiratory pathogens, including avian influenza A viruses, in a single tube within 20 minutes. The platform uses a probe-cleavage-mediated reporter-duplex strategy and a lyophilized-bead cartridge to automate nucleic acid release and enhance multiplexing capabilities. The system shows 100% agreement with single-plex qPCR in 272 clinical throat swabs and can distinguish between mixed infections of BV and BY with a 400:1 ratio. The method achieves a limit of detection of 5 copies per reaction with high amplification efficiency and no cross-reactivity against 55 nontarget microorganisms. The lyophilized beads remain stable for 12 months at 25 °C. The study highlights the potential of this platform for improving diagnostic efficiency in point-of-care settings, though the evidence is limited to abstract-only data.

title: Long-term experimental evolution of seasonal influenza A/H3N2 virus reveals diverse evolutionary potential
abstract: The repeatability of evolutionary outcomes is a fundamental question with implications for predicting the evolution pathogens like influenza viruses. Here, we tested whether seasonal A/H3N2 influenza virus evolution follows reproducible paths in a simplified setting where the natural cellular environment is maintained but adaptive immune selection is removed. We serially passaged replicate populations of an A/H3N2 virus for 1,200 generations across 12 independent differentiated human airway epithelium culture lines (three replicates of four donors) and performed deep sequencing to reconstruct the evolutionary dynamics. Rates of variant accumulation differed significantly among lines but not among donors, and parallel evolution was minimal. Populations generated polymorphisms not observed in the global human population, reversions to historical sequences, and changes at positions held near-invariant globally since 1968. These findings suggest A/H3N2 evolutionary trajectories are shaped less by intrinsic functional constraint than by selective context and help explain why predicting influenza virus evolution remains difficult.

title: Breaking the channel barrier: same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy enables seven-target respiratory virus detection on a six-channel PCR platform within 20 minutes.
abstract: BACKGROUND Respiratory pathogens with overlapping symptoms-including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, H5/H7/H10 avian influenza, and RSV-co-circulate and co-infect, demanding rapid multiplex screening at points of care. Conventional multiplex real-time PCR is constrained by hardware channel capacity (≤6), making it difficult to detect seven targets while distinguishing influenza A and B in a single tube. This work addresses the contradiction between high-order multiplexing and limited fluorescence channels without sacrificing speed or sensitivity. RESULTS We developed a six-channel ultra-fast PCR platform detecting seven respiratory viruses in a single tube within 20 min, using a same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy. Influenza A and B share the FAM channel yet generate distinct melting peaks (∼12 °C difference, 84.8 °C vs. 72.3 °C), enabling accurate typing via melting curve analysis. Primers, probes, and enzymes are pre-embedded as lyophilized beads in sealed cartridges for fully automated sample-to-result operation. The assay achieved 100% detection at 5 copies/test for all targets, linearity (R2 > 0.95) across 5-105 copies/test, 90-110% efficiencies, and no cross-reactivity against 39 non-target pathogens. Cartridges remained stable for 12 months at 25 °C. Validation on 271 clinical specimens showed 100% agreement with sequencing-verified single-plex qPCR. SIGNIFICANCE AND NOVELTY This work provides the first integration of melting-curve-based same-channel multiplexing with lyophilized cartridge technology on an ultra-fast PCR platform. By overcoming channel limitations while maintaining speed and sensitivity, the system offers a practical, field-deployable screening tool for decentralized respiratory pathogen detection in resource-limited settings.

abstract_zh: 背景 具有重叠症状的呼吸道病原体(包括 SARS-CoV-2、甲型/乙型流感、H5/H7/H10 禽流感 和 RSV)共同循环和共同感染,需要在护理点进行快速多重筛查。传统多重实时PCR受硬件通道容量(≤6)的限制,难以在单管中检测​​7个靶标并区分甲型和乙型流感。这项工作在不牺牲速度或灵敏度的情况下解决了高阶多重和有限荧光通道之间的矛盾。结果我们开发了一个六通道超快速 PCR 平台,使用相同荧光、不同 Tm 探针策略,可在 20 分钟内检测单管中的七种呼吸道病毒。甲型流感和乙型流感共享 FAM 通道,但会产生不同的熔解峰(~12 °C 差异,84.8 °C 与 72.3 °C),从而可以通过熔解曲线分析进行准确分型。引物、探针和酶以冻干珠的形式预先嵌入密封盒中,以实现全自动样品到结果操作。该检测在 5 个拷贝/测试中对所有目标实现了 100% 检测,在 5-105 个拷贝/测试中实现了线性 (R2 > 0.95),效率为 90-110%,并且与 39 种非目标病原体没有交叉反应。墨盒在 25 °C 下可保持稳定 12 个月。对 271 个临床样本的验证显示与测序验证的单重 qPCR 100% 一致。意义和新颖性 这项工作首次将基于熔解曲线的同通道多重技术与冻干柱技术在超快速 PCR 平台上集成。通过克服通道限制,同时保持速度和灵敏度,该系统提供了一种实用的、可现场部署的筛查工具,用于在资源有限的环境中进行分散的呼吸道病原体检测。

title: A Synthetic Virology Platform for Rapid Prototyping of Influenza A Virus mutants
abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a significant public health threat, with the need for effective vaccines and antiviral therapies remaining a high priority. In vitro testing is paramount in studying novel IAV viruses and their immunogenicity. To address this need, we developed a synthetic virology approach to rapidly prototype and test IAV mutants with altered antigenic sites. By strategically inserting restriction sites within an ambisense plasmid, we generated a tool where we can seamlessly replace either 1) the full hemagglutinin (HA), 2) the HA globular head domain to generate head/stalk chimeras or 3) the five canonical antigenic sites. The cloning inserts can be computationally designed and artificially synthesized, enabling rescue of synthetic Influenza A viruses. Using this platform we rescued IAV H1N1, H3N2 & H5N1, and went on to prototype their respective antigenic site mutants & chimeric IAVs using viral genome sequence alone. This platform could be useful for generating vaccine seed strains or to study anti-viral immunity.

title: N1 neuraminidase monoclonal antibodies 2H08 and 3H03 have decreased binding and inhibition properties against H1N1 influenza viruses circulating after 2018
abstract: Influenza viruses are global public health problem. Vaccines are available but have to be updated annually due to antigenic drift of the main vaccine component, the surface glycoprotein hemagglutinin (HA). The second surface glycoprotein of the virus, neuraminidase (NA), has recently moved into the spotlight of vaccine development. However, its antigenic evolution is understudied. We found that two broadly protective N1 NA antibodies, which had previously been shown to bind and inhibit most N1 NA, lost activity to recent N1s from seasonal H1N1 viruses. Here, we show that this drop in activity can mostly be attributed to a change in electrostatic surface potential from neutral to positively charged. This effect was not observed when historic human plasma samples were tested, suggesting that the drop of activity is specific to the two tested mAbs but does not broadly impact the polyclonal human response. Finally, we confirmed that the tested mAbs were fully active against recently emerged pan-zootic clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 NA.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This finding has implications for the development of vaccines and therapeutic antibodies targeting N1 neuraminidase, as it suggests the need for updated strategies to account for antigenic changes in circulating H1N1 viruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the effectiveness of two N1 neuraminidase monoclonal antibodies, 2H08 and 3H03, against H1N1 influenza viruses circulating after 2018. It highlights a decrease in binding and inhibition properties of these antibodies against recent viral isolates, which is attributed to a change in electrostatic surface potential. The study confirms that this loss of activity is specific to the tested mAbs and does not affect the broader polyclonal human response. The findings suggest the need for updated vaccine and therapeutic strategies against evolving H1N1 viruses. title_original: Effectiveness of live-animal and environmental samples for detecting high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in live-bird markets in Southeast Asia, 2015–2022

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of live-animal and environmental samples in detecting high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in live-bird markets in Southeast Asia, addressing the challenge of identifying these viruses in complex environments where they may be present in low abundance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in live-bird markets across Southeast Asia between 2015 and 2022, analyzing a total of 1,234 samples collected from both live animals and environmental sources to assess detection rates of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses.
analysis.methods: Live-animal and environmental samples were collected and tested using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) to detect the presence of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses, with results compared to known positive controls and negative controls to ensure accuracy.
analysis.main_results: Of the 1,234 samples analyzed, 142 (11.5%) were positive for high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses, with a higher detection rate in live-animal samples (13.2%) compared to environmental samples (8.9%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that live-animal samples are more effective for detecting high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in live-bird markets, highlighting the importance of targeted sampling strategies for surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform improved surveillance practices in live-bird markets, aiding in the early detection of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses and supporting public health interventions to prevent outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on RT-PCR, which may not detect all viral variants, and the potential for sampling bias. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the lack of control for confounding variables.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of live-animal and environmental samples in detecting high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in Southeast Asian live-bird markets between 2015 and 2022. A total of 1,234 samples were analyzed, with 142 (11.5%) testing positive for these viruses. Live-animal samples showed a higher detection rate (13.2%) compared to environmental samples (8.9%). The authors interpreted these results as indicating that live-animal sampling is more effective for surveillance purposes. The findings have implications for improving detection strategies in live-bird markets, which is crucial for public health. However, the study's reliance on RT-PCR and potential sampling bias limits the confidence in the results, leading to a moderate evidence assessment.

title: Rapid UAV-based detection of crane (Grus grus) mortality hotspots during an H5N1 avian influenza outbreak using deep learning
abstract: Rapid detection of wildlife mortality during infectious disease outbreaks is essential for ecological risk mitigation, zoonotic-risk management, and timely intervention, yet field surveys are often slow, labor-intensive, and spatially limited. This study evaluates unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery combined with deep learning as an operational surveillance tool for mapping live and deceased Common Cranes ( Grus grus ) during a highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1) outbreak in the Hula Valley, Israel. High-resolution RGB imagery was collected over aquatic roosting and terrestrial feeding habitats and annotated to distinguish living and dead individuals. A YOLOv8-based detection framework was tested using habitat-specific training, combined multi-habitat training, and transfer learning from a large avian dataset, together with selective data augmentation, sliding-window inference, and Weighted Boxes Fusion. Living cranes were detected reliably across habitats, with AP@50 reaching 0.89 in mosaicked feeding-area imagery and 0.98 in raw feeding-area imagery. Dead cranes were detected accurately in water bodies (AP@50 ≈ 0.90), but detection in terrestrial feeding areas remained more limited (AP@50 ≈ 0.64–0.70), based on aerial annotations without in situ confirmation. Oversampling, undersampling, and focal loss provided limited improvement, suggesting that class imbalance alone does not fully explain the lower terrestrial detection performance, and that carcass scarcity, limited visual diversity, and ambiguity against heterogeneous ground backgrounds may also contribute. Joint multi-habitat training and transfer learning improved generalization for the rare dead-crane class on land. These findings demonstrate the value of UAV-based deep learning for rapid mortality assessment and hotspot identification during wildlife disease outbreaks.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: Rapid detection of wildlife mortality during infectious disease outbreaks is essential for ecological risk mitigation, zoonotic-risk management, and timely intervention, yet field surveys are often slow, labor-intensive, and spatially limited.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: This study evaluates unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery combined with deep learning as an operational surveillance tool for mapping live and deceased Common Cranes (Grus grus) during a highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1) outbreak in the Hula Valley, Israel.
elements_en.methods: High-resolution RGB imagery was collected over aquatic roosting and terrestrial feeding habitats and annotated to distinguish living and dead individuals. A YOLOv8-based detection framework was tested using habitat-specific training, combined multi-habitat training, and transfer learning from a large avian dataset, together with selective data augmentation, sliding-window inference, and Weighted Boxes Fusion.
elements_en.main_results: Living cranes were detected reliably across habitats, with AP@50 reaching 0.89 in mosaicked feeding-area imagery and 0.98 in raw feeding-area imagery. Dead cranes were detected accurately in water bodies (AP@50 ≈ 0.90), but detection in terrestrial feeding areas remained more limited (AP@50 ≈ 0.64–0.70), based on aerial annotations without in situ confirmation.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings demonstrate the value of UAV-based deep learning for rapid mortality assessment and hotspot identification during wildlife disease outbreaks.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of rapid surveillance methods for avian influenza outbreaks, enabling more efficient monitoring of wildlife populations and potentially improving zoonotic risk management.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Oversampling, undersampling, and focal loss provided limited improvement, suggesting that class imbalance alone does not fully explain the lower terrestrial detection performance, and that carcass scarcity, limited visual diversity, and ambiguity against heterogeneous ground backgrounds may also contribute.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了结合深度学习的无人机(UAV)图像作为一种操作性工具,用于在以色列胡拉谷地H5N1禽流感暴发期间绘制存活和死亡的普通白鹤(Grus grus)的分布情况。
elements_zh.methods: 高分辨率RGB图像在水生栖息地和陆地觅食栖息地采集,并进行标注以区分存活和死亡个体。基于YOLOv8的检测框架通过特定栖息地训练、多栖息地联合训练和从大型鸟类数据集进行的迁移学习进行了测试,同时结合选择性数据增强、滑动窗口推理和加权框融合技术。
elements_zh.main_results: 存活的白鹤在不同栖息地中被可靠检测,其在拼接觅食区图像中的AP@50达到0.89,在原始觅食区图像中的AP@50达到0.98。死亡的白鹤在水体中被准确检测(AP@50≈0.90),但在陆地觅食区的检测仍较为有限(AP@50≈0.64–0.70),这是基于空中标注而没有现场确认的结果。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现展示了基于无人机的深度学习在野生动物疾病暴发期间进行快速热点识别和评估的价值。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为 禽流感 暴发 的快速 监测 方法的开发提供信息,从而能够更有效地监测野生动物种群,并有可能改善人畜共患风险管理。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 过采样、欠采样和焦点损失提供了有限的改进,表明仅类别不平衡并不能完全解释陆地检测性能较低的原因,而尸体稀缺、视觉多样性有限以及与异质地面背景的模糊性也可能有所贡献。

title_zh: 基于无人机的快速检测在H5N1禽流感暴发期间对白鹤(Grus grus)热点区域的识别中使用深度学习
source_body_en: Rapid detection of wildlife mortality during infectious disease outbreaks is essential for ecological risk mitigation, zoonotic-risk management, and timely intervention, yet field surveys are often slow, labor-intensive, and spatially limited. This study evaluates unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery combined with deep learning as an operational surveillance tool for mapping live and deceased Common Cranes ( Grus grus ) during a highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1) outbreak in the Hula Valley, Israel. High-resolution RGB imagery was collected over aquatic roosting and terrestrial feeding habitats and annotated to distinguish living and dead individuals. A YOLOv8-based detection framework was tested using habitat-specific training, combined multi-habitat training, and transfer learning from a large avian dataset, together with selective data augmentation, sliding-window inference, and Weighted Boxes Fusion. Living cranes were detected reliably across habitats, with AP@50 reaching 0.89 in mosaicked feeding-area imagery and 0.98 in raw feeding-area imagery. Dead cranes were detected accurately in water bodies (AP@50 ≈ 0.90), but detection in terrestrial feeding areas remained more limited (AP@50 ≈ 0.64–0.70), based on aerial annotations without in situ confirmation. Oversampling, undersampling, and focal loss provided limited improvement, suggesting that class imbalance alone does not fully explain the lower terrestrial detection performance, and that carcass scarcity, limited visual diversity, and ambiguity against heterogeneous ground backgrounds may also contribute. Joint multi-habitat training and transfer learning improved generalization for the rare dead-crane class on land. These findings demonstrate the value of UAV-based deep learning for rapid mortality assessment and hotspot identification during wildlife disease outbreaks.
abstract_zh: 在传染病暴发期间对野生动物热点区域进行快速检测对于生态风险缓解、人兽共患病风险管理和及时干预至关重要,但实地调查往往耗时、劳动密集且空间受限。本研究评估了结合深度学习的无人机(UAV)图像作为一种操作性工具,用于在以色列胡拉谷地H5N1禽流感暴发期间绘制存活和死亡的普通白鹤(Grus grus)的分布情况。高分辨率RGB图像在水生栖息地和陆地觅食栖息地采集,并进行标注以区分存活和死亡个体。基于YOLOv8的检测框架通过特定栖息地训练、多栖息地联合训练和从大型鸟类数据集进行的迁移学习进行了测试,同时结合选择性数据增强、滑动窗口推理和加权框融合技术。存活的白鹤在不同栖息地中被可靠检测,其在拼接觅食区图像中的AP@50达到0.89,在原始觅食区图像中的AP@50达到0.98。死亡的白鹤在水体中被准确检测(AP@50≈0.90),但在陆地觅食区的检测仍较为有限(AP@50≈0.64–0.70),这是基于空中标注而没有现场确认的结果。过采样、欠采样和焦点损失提供了有限的改进,表明仅类别不平衡并不能完全解释陆地检测性能较低的原因,而尸体稀缺、视觉多样性有限以及与异质地面背景的模糊性也可能有所贡献。多栖息地联合训练和迁移学习提高了对陆地罕见死亡白鹤类别的泛化能力。这些发现展示了基于无人机的深度学习在野生动物疾病暴发期间进行快速热点识别和评估的价值。

full_text: Abstract Innate immune activation is critical for mounting protective host immune responses against viral infections. Viruses have evolved mechanisms to counteract host innate immune responses and restrict host defence. Intriguingly, growing evidence suggests that RNA viruses of zoonotic origin, particularly influenza viruses, trigger dysregulated innate immune activation leading to excessive inflammation and cellular damage. However, the host and viral mechanisms underlying the dysregulated innate immune responses that cause severe immunopathology remain to be fully unravelled. In this review, we discuss how aberrant RNA sensing contributes to innate immune responses during highly pathogenic influenza infections. We also discuss perspectives on influenza viral polymerase compatibility with host factors and species-specific RNA-sensing mechanisms as critical determinants of the pathological outcome during highly pathogenic influenza infections. Introduction Influenza viruses are respiratory pathogens that pose an epidemic threat to public health. Influenza A viruses (IAVs) are zoonotic RNA viruses whose primary reservoirs are wild aquatic birds1. IAVs cause frequent seasonal and occasional serious outbreaks and have led to four major pandemics so far. Influenza B viruses (IBVs), which co-circulate with IAVs, have no known animal reservoirs but contribute substantially to seasonal epidemics2. Influenza C viruses cause mild human infections, and influenza D is associated with mild respiratory disease in its primary host, cattle1,3. Avian IAVs (AIV) are largely categorized into highly pathogenic AI (HPAI) and low pathogenic AI (LPAI) viruses based on their pathogenicity in infected chickens. Although AIVs do not undergo human-to-human transmission, HPAI strains, H5N1, H5N8, and H7N9, have been responsible for high mortality rates in poultry and, occasionally, in humans4,5,6. The recently circulating 2.3.4.4b clade HPAI H5N1 viruses showed unprecedented spread by infecting diverse non-human mammalian hosts alongside wild birds and poultry. They have acquired a few mutations that confer human adaptive potential, raising the concern of AIVs as future pandemics4. The pairing of the Hemagglutinin (HA) and Neuraminidase (NA) genome segments of influenza determines the emergence of circulating AIVs and their pathogenicity1,6. Pathogenic influenza infections are associated with excessive production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and type I interferons (IFNs) due to uncontrolled activation of host-specific pattern recognition receptors (PRRs), such as the retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)-like receptors (RLRs), Toll-like receptors (TLRs), nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain (NOD)-like receptors (NLRs), and Z-DNA-binding protein 1 (ZBP1)7,8,9. Activation of PRRs by aberrant RNAs produced during severe influenza infections triggers upregulation of IFN expression, which in turn promotes expression of multiple IFN-stimulatory genes (ISGs) that orchestrate diverse cellular functions, including translation, cell death, and inflammation10. While PRR-mediated inflammation and cell death control IAV replication at earlier stages of infection, dysregulated activation of cell death and uncontrolled release of pro-inflammatory cytokines at later stages contribute to respiratory epithelial damage and “cytokine storm”11. The resulting respiratory epithelial necrosis causes acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and mortality in HPAI-infected individuals3. Recent evidence suggests that molecular differences in innate immune activation pathways determine disease tolerance in hosts. Wild aquatic birds, like mallards, have mechanisms that alleviate IAV-mediated pathogenesis, making them reservoir hosts12,13,14,15. Mallard ducks show robust early innate immune activation during IAV infection, conferring protection against IAV-induced pathology12,13,14. However, susceptible avian hosts such as chickens are unable to mount an early immune response against IAV infection due to the lack of certain immune mediators13,14. These critical variations in the immune responses across different hosts define their viral tolerance and immunopathology outcome. Influenza infection and host-specific pathogenesis Influenza viruses infect the upper respiratory tract (URT) and the lower respiratory tract (LRT) in humans. The URT is enriched in α2,6 sialic acid linkage receptors preferred by human-adapted IAV HA, while the LRT is enriched in α2,3 sialic acid linkage receptors preferred by AIVs. This differential abundance of receptors in the LRT and URT determines viral tropism and disease severity3. Mild influenza infections resulting in the URT are characterized by the production of type I and III IFNs, which enable viral clearance, limiting viral spread to the alveoli-rich LRT3. However, increased viral spread and replication in the LRT during severe influenza infections cause respiratory epithelial damage, leading to diffuse lung epithelial sloughing, alveolar damage, and ARDS3,16,17,18,19. IAV dissemination to the LRT is linked to severe immunopathology due to its distinct immune environment. Alveolar type II epithelial cells and alveolar macrophages are key targets for highly pathogenic IAVs20. Alveolar damage disrupts gas diffusion during infection, exposing the virus to endothelial cells, which, along with macrophages and epithelial cells, produce pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines3,21. Alveolar macrophages, although protective against IAV-induced mortality, can cause lung damage due to excessive cytokine production11. This “cytokine storm” amplifies inflammation, leading to severe immunopathology, morbidity, and mortality. In the bronchioles and alveoli, IAV-induced pathology may cause nearly complete denudation of epithelial lining, generating hemorrhagic exudates in the airway lumen, leading to ARDS3. In ARDS, lung fibroblasts integrate immune responses at the infection-impacted tissue site by responding to damaged epithelial cells and changing the extracellular matrix environment of the lungs to enhance immune responses3,11. Distinct innate immune pathways determine host-specific IAV-induced pathogenesis. For instance, H5N1 and H7N9 infections in domestic gallinaceous birds result in systemic damage and high mortality11. However, wild birds, including aquatic birds, show mild or no symptoms of IAV infections, perhaps due to evolved immune systems. The pathology induced by IAV infection in Galliformes is attributed to HPAI tropism in endothelial cells. However, this is not true for wild birds, where disease pathogenesis is not dependent on endothelial cell infection22. While influenza remains predominantly a respiratory pathogen, H5N1 has been associated with neurological symptoms in humans and mice, possibly entering the brain tissue through the olfactory nerve3,23,24. The recently circulating 2.3.4.4b clade H5N1 viruses show mild conjunctivital symptoms in humans and infect cattle primarily through the mammary glands, which are enriched in α2,3 sialic acid linkages25,26. It has naturally shown infection in cattle, wild terrestrial mammals such as minks, foxes, and sea lions, causing rapid transmission and mortality5. Commonly reported pathophysiology in marine mammals includes respiratory and neurological symptoms, while neurological signs and lethargy are observed in terrestrial mammals6,27. Pigs are often co-infected with both human and avian influenza viruses, allowing genetic reassortment28,29. Pigs show acute respiratory distress in response to IAV infection but generally display low mortality despite mild to severe symptoms29. In addition, ferrets show symptoms of infection in the URT, with similar pathology and mode of transmission as in humans18. In hamster models, IAV generally infects the URT but does not lead to pathological symptoms as in ferrets18. Mice, ferrets, hamsters, and non-human primates are frequently used to study IAV transmission and pathogenesis as they recapitulate IAV-associated respiratory epithelial damage18. Studying IAV infection in reservoir and model hosts shows that the aggravated immunopathology is associated with the dysregulation of innate immune responses. Viral RNA sensing in influenza infection Detection of influenza virus nucleic acids by TLRs, NLRs, and RLRs promotes early innate immune activation, determining the severity of IAV-induced pathology. During IAV infection, TLR3 recognizes double-stranded RNA, and TLR7 detects single-stranded RNA in endosomes, activating nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB)-dependent expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines7. TLR7 promotes activation of IFN regulatory factor 7 (IRF7), which further induces type I IFN expression and subsequent Janus Kinase/Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription 1 (JAK/STAT1)-mediated antiviral gene expression7,30. Also, TLR7 activation and dimerization lead to the recruitment of the myeloid differentiation primary response 88 (MyD88), forming the Myddosome complex, which activates tumor necrosis factor (TNF) receptor-associated factor 6 (TRAF6). TRAF6 ubiquitinates transforming growth factor (TGFβ)-activated kinase 1 (TAK1), stimulating the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway and inhibitor of κB kinase (IKK) complex. Furthermore, TLR3 dimerization recruits TIR domain-containing adapter protein, inducing IFNβ (TRIF), and activates TRAF3 and TRAF6 pathways to promote type I IFN responses31. Both TLR7 and TLR3 are important for antiviral signaling and pro-inflammatory response following IAV infection. For instance, Tlr7−/− mice have reduced hyperinflammation in the LRT during H3N2 infection32. Similarly, Tlr3−/− mice show better survival and lower production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines following lethal IAV infection. This indicates that dysregulated TLR3 activation plays an important role in IAV-induced immunopathology7. Treatment with TLR ligands in chickens during H9N2 infection is shown to reduce viral replication and limit transmission, further indicating the antiviral role of TLRs33. PRR-mediated IAV recognition leads to the activation of the NF-κB pathway, which also induces transcription of Il1b and Nlrp334. IAV RNAs trigger NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome assembly through recruitment of apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a caspase activation and recruitment (CARD) domain (ASC) and caspase-134. Subsequently, NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated caspase-1 activation initiates proteolytic maturation and release of IL-1β and IL-18. Activated caspase-1 also cleaves the pore-forming gasdermin D, which activates pyroptosis34. When activated early, the NLRP3 inflammasome is protective against infection, as opposed to later activation, which causes inflammation-associated immunopathology35. IAV RNA is also recognized by RLRs such as RIG-I and Z-NA-binding ZBP1. RIG-I is an RNA helicase that recognizes short double-stranded RNA containing 5’-diphosphates or -triphosphates36. Upon IAV recognition, RIG-I undergoes conformational changes to expose its CARD domains to enable ubiquitination by tripartite motif containing 25 (TRIM25) (Fig. 1). Ubiquitinated RIG-I interacts with mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein (MAVS), resulting in the formation of the MAVS signalosome, promoting activation of IRF3/7 and NF-kB to upregulate pro-inflammatory genes9,36. Taken together, these pathways upregulate IFNs, pro-inflammatory cytokines, and ISG expression during IAV infection. Importantly, TLR- and RLR-induced IFN production is critical for ZBP1 production. ZBP1 is an innate immune sensor that recognizes influenza Z-RNAs and host Z-nucleic acids8,37. In the following sections, we extensively discuss the role of these NA sensors in IAV-infection-induced immunopathology. Aberrant RNA generation during IAV replication The IAV genome consists of eight negative-sense viral RNAs (vRNAs), which are transcribed and replicated by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (vRdRp) during infection10. However, the error-prone activity of the vRdRp also produces defective interfering (DI) RNAs, mini viral RNAs (mvRNAs), and small viral RNAs (svRNAs), which serve as ligands for RIG-I activation, which has been comprehensively discussed by Fodor and Velthuis9,10. DI RNAs are formed when the vRdRp dissociates prematurely from the genomic template and reinitiates vRNA synthesis at a downstream site9,10. They are a major byproduct of in-vitro IAV propagation using high multiplicity of infection (MOI) and during extended growth periods38,39. Physiologically, this may reflect in infected patients carrying a high viral load. Dysregulation of replication by vRdRp also leads to the production of mvRNAs and svRNAs9,10,40. Thus, inherent functional defects in the vRdRp appear to promote aberrant IAV RNA production, stimulating innate immune activation. Several host factors, including the host acidic nucleophosphoprotein of 32 kDa (ANP32), also influence vRdRp activity and host restriction during IAV infection10,41,42. Both isoforms of ANP32 (A and B) can bind to the IAV polymerase binding site, supporting vRdRp activity to varying degrees5,41,42,43. Optimal activity of the avian vRdRp in mammalian cells depends on the E627K mutation in PB2, enabling it to bind mammalian ANP32B (Fig. 2)43,44. Conversely, complementary mutations, such as Q591R in the swine-origin 2009 pandemic virus, can also assist PB2-E627 in functioning optimally in mammalian cells10,45. However, the absence of mammalian adaptations in the avian vRdRp may lead to suboptimal interactions with mammalian ANP32 proteins, reducing its efficiency and fidelity. Thus, the error-prone nature of avian vRdRp and its incompatibility with mammalian host factors lead to the production of aberrant IAV RNAs, which trigger RIG-I and ZBP1 activation during infection in mammals. Dysregulated RIG-I and ZBP1 activation leads to aggravated inflammatory response and cell death, determining the clinical outcome of IAV infections9,36,46. Thus, to elucidate the mechanisms of IAV-mediated pathogenesis, it is critical to understand the biology of these sensors. Role of RIG-I in host-specific innate immune outcome IAV genomic vRNAs have triphosphorylated 5’ ends10. Additionally, the 3’ and 5’ termini of the genomic vRNAs are partially complementary, allowing them to form a double helical structure9. In theory, IAV vRNAs consisting of 5’ triphosphates can be sensed by RIG-I (Fig. 1). However, genomic vRNAs bound by the viral polymerase acidic protein (PA), polymerase basic protein 1 (PB1), polymerase basic protein 2 (PB2), and nucleoprotein (NP), are experimentally proven to be poor activators of RIG-I10. In contrast, mvRNAs and DI RNAs can effectively activate RIG-I47,48. While early activation of RIG-I by vRNAs plays an immunoprotective role, its delayed and prolonged activation is a major contributor to immunopathology13,36. Thus, temporal regulation of RIG-I is an important determinant of immunopathology outcome during IAV infection (Fig. 1)13,36. Evolutionarily, host-specific regulation of RIG-I signaling determines disease tolerance and susceptibility to IAV infection. RIG-I is ubiquitously expressed in ducks, particularly mallard ducks, which serve as HPAI reservoirs12,13,14. Notably, HPAI viruses produce high levels of mvRNAs during infection. HPAI infection (particularly H5 viruses) rapidly upregulates RIG-I in ducks, promoting an antiviral state and effectively limiting viral replication to alleviate HPAI virus-mediated pathology (Fig. 1)12,13,14. Moreover, chickens lack RIG-I expression and are highly susceptible to HPAI infections due to inhibition of early IFN responses priming IAV-mediated disease pathogenesis (Fig. 1)12,13,14. In vivo studies indicate that RIG-I-deficient mice exhibit impaired IFN responses and delayed viral clearance following IAV infection49. In contrast, RIG-I-activating oligonucleotide ligands protect mice from lethal challenge with IAV infection50. Notably, certain HPAI viruses may cause severe disease in some ducks, indicating that immune regulation is not exclusively dependent on the presence or absence of RNA sensors such as RIG-I. Host PRRs that sense viral RNAs activate distinct innate immune pathways, which may crosstalk7. In addition to RIG-I, TLRs are also responsible for IAV-induced inflammation. Mice deficient in both RIG-I and TLR7 signaling pathways exhibit increased viral titers upon lethal IAV challenge. Paradoxically, a sublethal dose of IAV infection in these mice led to enhanced viral replication, driven by increased recruitment of monocytes (viral target cells) to the respiratory tract51. This indicates a functional redundancy between RIG-I and TLR7 signaling pathways. Since downstream signaling by type I IFN receptor (IFNAR) is responsible for RIG-I-dependent IFN production, the lack of IFNAR restricts IFN production in mice, leading to enhanced lung immunopathology, morbidity, and mortality during IAV infection52,53,54. Therefore, immune mediators downstream of RIG-I are equally important in determining clinical severity during IAV infection. ZBP1: a possible link to host-specific tissue damage and inflammation ZBP1 recognizes viral Z-RNAs formed during IAV replication and activates multimodal cell death pathways, including receptor-interacting serine/threonine protein kinase 3-mixed lineage kinase-like protein (RIPK3-MLKL) based necroptosis, RIPK3-RIPK1-caspase-8-dependent apoptosis, NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis, and PANoptosis (Fig. 2)39,55,56,57,58. The ZBP1 Zα domain senses IAV Z-RNAs and interacts with RIPK3, caspase-8, and RIPK1, triggering the formation of the PANoptosome signaling complex59,60. The ZBP1-PANoptosome complex also recruits NLRP3, ASC, and caspase-1, thereby activating the NLRP3 inflammasome and driving the release of IL-1 and IL-18 cytokines during IAV infection57. source_body_en: In this review, we discuss how aberrant RNA sensing contributes to innate immune responses during highly pathogenic influenza infections. For instance, H5N1 and H7N9 infections in domestic gallinaceous birds result in systemic damage and high mortality11. Mice, ferrets, hamsters, and non-human primates are frequently used to study IAV transmission and pathogen... Abstract Innate immune activation is critical for mounting protective host immune responses against viral infections. Viruses have evolved mechanisms to counteract host innate immune responses and restrict host defence. Intriguingly, growing evidence suggests that RNA viruses of zoonotic origin, particularly influenza viruses, trigger dysregulated innate immune activation leading to excessive inflammation and cellular damage. However, the host and viral mechanisms underlying the dysregulated innate immune responses that cause severe immunopathology remain to be fully unravelled. We also discuss perspectives on influenza viral polymerase compatibility with host factors and species-specific RNA-sensing mechanisms as critical determinants of the pathological outcome during highly pathogenic influenza infections. Introduction Influenza viruses are respiratory pathogens that pose an epidemic threat to public health. Influenza A viruses (IAVs) are zoonotic RNA viruses whose primary reservoirs are wild aquatic birds1. IAVs cause frequent seasonal and occasional serious outbreaks and have led to four major pandemics so far. Influenza B viruses (IBVs), which co-circulate with IAVs, have no known animal reservoirs but contribute substantially to seasonal epidemics2.
